title: High CPU — Symptom of Error Retry Loop
description: CPU usage is elevated because error_spike causes 30% of requests to return 500, which triggers aggressive client retries. The CPU burn thread models the server-side load of processing those retries. CPU is the *symptom* — error_spike is the *root cause*.

true_root_cause.summary: 30% of requests fail with HTTP 500 (error_spike=true, rate=0.3), causing client retry storms that drive up CPU usage

key_evidence_signals.expected_behaviour: Error rate spikes — ~30% of requests are HTTP 500
CPU rises — but this is a consequence of retry load, not the root cause
Latency is NOT significantly elevated — errors fail fast, before DB is touched
Ratio is stable — errors are thrown before DB queries run

red_herrings: High CPU is visible — naive diagnosis blames CPU contention or a CPU-bound workload
Correct diagnosis requires correlating CPU rise with error_rate rise, not with latency
recommended_fix: Identify and fix the error_spike source (application bug or downstream dependency); CPU normalises automatically once errors drop
evaluation_checks: Agent identifies error_spike as the root cause flag, NOT high_cpu
Agent cites http_errors_total as the primary evidence
Agent explains CPU rise as a consequence of retry storms
Agent does NOT recommend CPU scaling as a fix
